definition: In the KJV, a carved wooden pole or image of the goddess Asherah set up near an altar for idol worship. It is not a wood of living trees.
The way a person lives or behaves, as in riotous living.
The day of preparation, the Friday on which food and work were made ready before the sabbath or a feast.
In the KJV, a howling wild animal of ruins and wastelands, most often the jackal. It is not a fire-breathing monster.
In the KJV, ritually unclean or not sanctified for God, as food or people considered profane.
One of the four corners or sides of a garment.
Sure knowledge; certainty. To know of a surety is to know for certain.
A curtain or cloth screen hung as a door covering or wall, as in the tabernacle court.
In the heave offering, a portion of a sacrifice or produce lifted up and set apart as a gift to God and the priests.
A reason or opening used to accuse or attack someone, as in to seek occasion against a person.
